items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: So he ought to devote himself to his time to the subject he teaches in Howard and leave this part up to somebody who knows. He was a little bit of a piece of advice for Duke Ellington, he didn't come on the scene until 1927.

ctx.x: I know William Marion Cook personally. I knew it. Fine pianist, fine arranging, fine violinist, and a scat if you just commit one error in his music, especially in the pit. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah. You see? And then there were other things about the Negro and ragtime and jazz which a few writers have disqualified, but not so. You see, the top orchestra in New York at that time was Mary Wayne and Mary Anderson and Mary Lucas because they could go to the Union and resurrect 25 pieces of hair for an occasion right out of…
